args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the latest deploy (v2.3.1), running in us-east, us-west and eu-west with an error rate of ~18%. The previous v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy. The SRE agent rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent healthy release, in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). The rollback completed and was verified. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before any redeploy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions, and the service is healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

**What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, and about 18% of requests were failing.

**Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent healthy release. The release history isn't listed in order, but sorting by release number shows the two releases after v2.3.0 (v2.3.1-rc and v2.3.1) were both unhealthy, so I skipped them. Rolling back didn't need approval: that's only required for deploying a version that's never been healthy, and v2.3.0 has been.

**Result:** All three regions are on v2.3.0, health checks pass, and the error rate is down to about 0.2%.

**Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the result. It also notes that someone needs to find the cause of the v2.3.1 problem before it's redeployed.
